answer: One concrete defense ties an agent's standing to a single unbroken thread of attested work, not to raw headcount. Each identity starts on its own low knoll of near-zero trust, and reputation climbs only as independent peers co-sign its history. Because trust ripples outward slowly through that signed graph, spinning up a thousand fresh sybils buys nothing: none carry the costly, time-earned thread, so their rewards and votes stay flat.
